        "exact_quote": "Let $\\mathcal A\\subset(\\mathbb Q_{>0})^2$ be a finite list containing $(1,1)$ and $(1,25)$, and put $$\\mathcal U=\\mathcal A\n    \\cup\\{(u_1/2,u_2):(u_1,u_2)\\in\\mathcal A\\}\n    \\cup\\{(2u_1,u_2/2):(u_1,u_2)\\in\\mathcal A\\}.$$ Choose $K_0,M_0$ by Proposition <a href=\"#prop:trace-small-box\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prop:trace-small-box\">26</a> for $\\mathcal U$, with all displayed periods even and at least four. Let $\\omega_{\\beta_N}$ be the periodic infinite-plane state supplied by Section <a href=\"#sec:preliminary\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"sec:preliminary\">1</a>. There are constants $C,c>0$, independent of $N\\ge K_0$ and $k\\ge0$, with the following properties.*\n\n\n*For $(u_1,u_2)\\in\\mathcal A$, set $(n,w)=(u_1,u_2)2^kM_0L^N$. If a bounded local observable $F$ can be placed in a rectangle of time extent at most $n/2$ and spatial extent at most $w/2$, then $$|\\mu_{\\beta_N;n,w}(F)-\\omega_{\\beta_N}(F)|\n       \\le C\\left\\lVert F\\right\\rVert_\\infty e^{-c2^k}.\n \\label{eq:trace-uniform-volume}$$ The same estimate holds for a torus obtained by closing time with any integer spatial translation, provided the support has a lift of time extent at most $n/2$ and spatial extent at most $w/2$.*\n\n\n*For bounded local observables $F,G$ on the plane whose supporting time slabs are separated by $d\\ge0$ transfer edges, $$|\\operatorname{Cov}_{\\omega_{\\beta_N}}(F,G)|\n    \\le\\left\\lVert F\\right\\rVert_\\infty\\left\\lVert G\\right\\rVert_\\infty\n       e^{-c d/(M_0L^N)}.\n \\label{eq:orig-26}$$ The constant in this last estimate may be taken to be $c=\\log2$.",

        "anchor": "stmt-prop-source-step",
        "exact_quote": "Consider an admitted source-free step of Section 4 from layer $j$ to layer $j-1$, with precise coupling $b\\in[H_j/2,2H_j]$, together with source lists satisfying Equation <a href=\"#eq:orig-27\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:orig-27\">[eq:orig-27]</a> and the normalization and support conditions above. The source-free output is exactly the output at zero source. No further source-dependent volume scalar is extracted.*\n\n\n*For two compatible inputs to a regular step, let $u,\\lambda,\n\\epsilon_h$ be the source-free discrepancies of Equation <a href=\"#eq:orig-5\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:orig-5\">[eq:orig-5]</a>. Let $u_s$ be a fixed positively weighted sum of the regular and covering source discrepancies divided by $R_j$ and $w_j$, respectively; the regular discrepancy is measured through order $k-1$, with absent records padded by zero. The weights can be chosen so that, for some $q_s<1$, $$\\begin{split}\n u_s'&\\le q_su_s+\n   C_L(\\log H_j)^D\n          \\bigl(u+\\epsilon_h+|\\lambda|/H_j\\bigr),\\\\\n |c_{2,j}-c_{1,j}|&\\le C_LR_j\n    \\left[u_s+(\\log H_j)^D\n          \\bigl(u+\\epsilon_h+|\\lambda|/H_j\\bigr)\\right].\n \\end{split}\n \\label{eq:orig-29}$$ These estimates hold in bulk and simultaneously on the compatible admitted periods.         "anchor": "stmt-lem-boundary-strips",
        "exact_quote": "Fix an order $n$, a bounded region $K\\subset\\mathbb R^2$, and a bounded axis rectangle $A$. Let $E_\\varepsilon=K\\cap\\{x:\\operatorname{dist}(x,\\partial A)<\\varepsilon\\}$. In the plane, uniformly in $N\\ge K_0$ and in the microscopic origin, $$S_{n,N}^{\\boldsymbol\\alpha}\n       (E_\\varepsilon\\times K^{n-1})\n       \\le C_{n,K,A}(\\varepsilon+a_N).\n \\label{eq:boundary-strip-bound}$$ The same estimate holds on the axis tori, with the sets interpreted in fixed bounded periodic charts. It also holds with any one insertion in the strip. Consequently continuum convergence extends to products of bounded axis-box indicators, to smooth approximations of these indicators, and to cell boxes whose boundaries converge to the given box boundaries.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-prop-os-reconstruction",
        "exact_quote": "The Schwinger functions $S_n$ reconstruct a tempered Wightman theory in $1+1$ dimensions with a three-component Hermitian scalar field. Its Hilbert space $\\mathcal H$ is positive, its fields are local, and its unitary representation of the Poincaré group satisfies the spectrum condition. The vacuum $\\Omega$ is unique and normalized. In the positive-time reflection realization of $\\mathcal H$, Euclidean time translations induce a strongly continuous semigroup $e^{-sH_{\\rm phys}}$, $s\\ge0$, with $H_{\\rm phys}\\ge0$ and $H_{\\rm phys}\\Omega=0$.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-prop-rg-input",
        "exact_quote": "For every type $P\\in\\{r,+,-\\}$, initialize the nearest-neighbor model as in Section 5. As long as the input couplings lie in their admitted bands, the exact observations produce representations with all renewed shape caps and the recursion $$b_{j-1}=b_j+\\alpha^P_{N-j}\n              +\\frac{\\kappa^P_{N-j}}{b_j}+\\Delta_j,\n \\qquad |\\Delta_j|\\le C_LH_j^{-1.05}.\n \\label{eq:offset-flow}$$ There are $C_L<\\infty$, $0<\\sigma_1<1$, and a number $\\kappa_\\infty$ such that $$|\\alpha_h^P+\\gamma|+|\\kappa_h^P-\\kappa_\\infty|\n       \\le C_L\\sigma_1^h \\qquad(h\\ge0).\n \\label{eq:offset-increment-convergence}$$ These sequences are independent of the precise running couplings, and remain fixed when $H$ is increased. The two inclined types have the same scalar sequences.*\n\n\n\n*On common ordinary steps, with discrepancy variables defined above, $$\\begin{aligned}\n u_{j-1}&\\le q u_j+C_L\\operatorname{poly}(H_j)\\epsilon_h\n                        +e_j|\\lambda_j|,\\nonumber\\\\\n |\\lambda_{j-1}-\\lambda_j|\n     &\\le C_Lu_j+C_L\\operatorname{poly}(H_j)\\epsilon_h\n                        +e_j|\\lambda_j|,\n & e_j&=C_L(\\log H_j)^C/H_j.\n \\label{eq:offset-weak-comparison}\n\\end{aligned}$$ If the histories share their last $m$ ordinary observations, $\\epsilon_h$ may be taken to be $r_0^m$, where $r_0=A_0/L^2$. The choices can be made with $$\\max\\{q,r_0\\}<\\rho<L^{-2+\\upsilon}<1\n \\label{eq:offset-contraction-width}$$ and strict spare width. Here $q$ and $\\rho$ are fixed bounds valid for every subsequent sufficiently large $H$. The corresponding free kernels and their lifts compare in the exponential kernel norms of Proposition <a href=\"#prop:free-bounds\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prop:free-bounds\">9</a> with the same history bound.",
        "source_id": "PM-215.1"
      },

        "exact_quote": "For $H$ sufficiently large, every depth $N\\ge1$, every type $P\\in\\{r,+,-\\}$, and every bare coupling $\\beta=\\vartheta_N+s$ with $|s|\\le R'$ give a strictly admitted trajectory. Uniformly over these choices, $$b_j=\\vartheta_j+D_j,\\qquad\n \\max_{0\\le j\\le N}|D_j|\\le C_{L,R'}.\n \\label{eq:offset-admission}$$ Moreover, $$\\begin{aligned}\n D_{j-1}-D_j&=\\alpha^P_{N-j}+\\gamma+E_{j,N},\\nonumber\\\\\n |E_{j,N}|&\\le C_L\\left[\n H_j^{-1.05}\n +H_j^{-2}\\bigl(\\log(2+H_j/H)+|D_j|\\bigr)\n +H_j^{-1}\\sigma_1^{N-j}\\right],\n \\label{eq:offset-error-recursion}\n\\end{aligned}$$ and $$\\sup_{N,P,\\,|s|\\le R'}\\sum_{j=1}^{N}|E_{j,N}|\n       =o_H(1).\n \\label{eq:offset-error-sum}$$ The constants in <a href=\"#eq:offset-admission\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:offset-admission\">[eq:offset-admission]</a> stay bounded as $H$ is increased, with all earlier parameters fixed.",

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-finite-beta",
        "exact_quote": "For every sufficiently large fixed $\\beta$, the periodic plane law $\\mu_\\beta$ exists and is translation and $O(3)$ invariant. Every component moment $$\\mathbb E_{\\mu_\\beta}\\prod_{r=1}^n q_{x_r}^{i_r},\n \\qquad x_r\\in\\mathbb Z^2,\\quad i_r\\in\\{1,2,3\\},$$ is nonnegative. If $$C_\\beta(x)=\\mathbb E_{\\mu_\\beta}[q_0^1q_x^1],\\qquad\n \\chi_\\beta=\\sum_{x\\in\\mathbb Z^2}C_\\beta(x),\\qquad\n \\xi_\\beta^2=\\frac{\\sum_x|x|^2C_\\beta(x)}{4\\chi_\\beta},$$ then both sums converge absolutely and $0<\\chi_\\beta,\\xi_\\beta<\\infty$, where $\\xi_\\beta$ is the positive square root.         "exact_quote": "Fix $L,R,R'$ and choose $H$ sufficiently large as in Proposition <a href=\"#prop:admission\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prop:admission\">45</a>. <a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Periodic thermodynamic state** ([source](#pm-h-4)): For each $\beta$ used below, write $\mu_\beta$ for the local limit of periodic square tori as their side lengths tend to infinity.
- **Canonical lattice scales** ([source](#eq:canonical-lattice-scales)): The lattice itself supplies two normalization constants. Put $$\label{eq:canonical-lattice-scales} C_\beta(x)=\mathbb E_{\mu_\beta}[q_0^1q_x^1],\qquad \chi_\beta=\sum_{x\in\mathbb Z^2}C_\beta(x),\qquad \xi_\beta^2=\frac{1}{4\chi_\beta} \sum_{x\in\mathbb Z^2}\|x\|^2 C_\beta(x).$$
- **Canonical smeared field** ([source](#eq:canonical-field)): For a vector test $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb R^3)$ define $$\label{eq:canonical-field} \Psi_\beta(f)=\frac{1}{\xi_\beta\sqrt{\chi_\beta}} \sum_{x\in\mathbb Z^2} f(x/\xi_\beta)\cdot q_x.$$
- **Free observation history** ([source](#setup:scales)): A *free history* records the scalar observations already performed, including their coordinate frames.
- **Endpoint density** ([source](#setup:endpoint-law)): An *endpoint density* is a layer-zero representation satisfying the preceding caps, with $b\in[H/2,2H]$, and with the bulk scalar removed.
- **Complete support** ([source](#pm-h-18)): The complete support contains every spin argument and every edge or site queried by a mask, an eligibility test, a test for the absence of another object, or a window used to determine the formula.
- **Winding record** ([source](#eq:setup-short-record)): All other records are called *winding*.
- **Quadratic coefficient-list norm** ([source](#eq:setup-quadratic-norm)): The norm of a quadratic list is the supremum over anchors of the sum of these contributions.
- **Terminal cell** ([source](#pm-h-64)): A terminal cell is the set of microscopic descendants of one layer-zero site in a standard blocking.
- **Relative two-point measure** ([source](#eq:relative-factorization)): We next pass from local convergence to susceptibility and second-moment length. Write $S_2^{\mathrm{cut}}$ for the first-component two-point measure of a run. In coordinates $(y_1,z)=(y_1,y_2-y_1)$, microscopic translation invariance gives the exact factorization $$S_2^{\mathrm{cut}}=\alpha_a\otimes\nu^{\mathrm{cut}},\qquad \alpha_a=a^2\sum_{x\in\mathbb Z^2}\delta_{aUx},\qquad \nu^{\mathrm{cut}}=B^2a^2\sum_{x\in\mathbb Z^2} C_\beta(x)\delta_{aUx}. \label{eq:relative-factorization}$$
- **Canonical normalized offset hierarchy** ([source](#stmt-prop-normalization)): (Canonical normalization at a fixed offset). *For every $s\in I$, the quantities $m(s)$ and $\ell(s)$ in <a href="#eq:offset-mass-length" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:offset-mass-length">[eq:offset-mass-length]</a> are finite and strictly positive. For an ordinary sequence with $N\to\infty$ and offset tending to $s$, $$B^2a^2\chi_\beta\longrightarrow m(s),\qquad a\xi_\beta\longrightarrow\ell(s). \label{eq:offset-cutoff-normalization}$$ For an inclined sequence with limiting offset $s$ and $s,s+d\in I$, the limits are $m(s+d)$ and $\ell(s+d)$.* *Define $G_s$ by applying to $F_s$ the change of smeared fields $$\phi(f)\longmapsto\frac{1}{\ell(s)\sqrt{m(s)}} \phi\bigl(f(\,\cdot/\ell(s))\bigr). \label{eq:canonical-hierarchy-normalization}$$
- **Rotation pushforward of a hierarchy** ([source](#sec:uniqueness)): For a rotation $U$ of the Euclidean plane, write $U_*G$ for the hierarchy obtained by pushing each insertion coordinate forward by $U$.

<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-initial-reduction** [claim](#stmt-lem-prelim-initial-reduction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-prelim-initial-reduction): Radial rotation estimates and spherical integration by parts. -> Strict initial stiffness saving.
- **step-stiffness-iteration** [claim](#stmt-lem-prelim-iteration) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-prelim-iteration): Conditional Gaussian augmentation and divergence-test variance gains. -> Small stiffness at a controlled larger side.
- **step-preliminary-mixing** [claim](#stmt-prop-preliminary) / [proof](#pm-h-12): Rotation comparison, disagreement exploration, conditional ferromagnetic decomposition, and bond interpolation. -> Uniform preliminary mixing and rectangular doubling.
- **step-inclined-geometry** [claim](#stmt-lem-free-inclined-geometry) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-free-inclined-geometry): Integral translation geometry and weighted coordinate paths. -> Connected cell partition and unit-mean error bound.
- **step-small-chord-mean** [claim](#stmt-cor-free-small-chord-mean) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-free-small-chord-mean): Weighted squared-pair identity. -> Forced normalized mean and quadratic error.
- **step-free-bounds** [claim](#stmt-prop-free-bounds) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-free-bounds): Alias decay, analytic denominator estimates, and common-tail comparison. -> Localized free operators and history contraction.
- **step-positive-completion** [claim](#stmt-prop-free-positive) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-free-positive): Analytic edge divisions and positive defect factorization. -> Covariant localized positive kinetic identities.
- **step-ambient-completion** [claim](#stmt-lem-rg-ambient) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-rg-ambient): Normalized auxiliary scalar and intrinsic chart change. -> Ambient Gaussian integral and controlled scalar error.
- **step-prediction** [claim](#stmt-lem-rg-prediction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-rg-prediction): First-tangent harmonic completion and localized kernel estimates. -> Spin prediction with suppressed fine gradients.
- **step-core-reserves** [claim](#stmt-lem-rg-reserves) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-rg-reserves): Positive-square charging and Gaussian tail splitting. -> Core and tail reserves with derivative envelopes.
- **step-joint-integration** [claim](#stmt-prop-rg-joint) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-rg-joint): Joint Gaussian majorants, hard-read transport, and marked interpolation. -> Product estimates and support factorization.
- **step-canonical-contraction** [claim](#stmt-lem-rg-canonical-contraction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-rg-canonical-contraction): Spatial expansion with affine compensation and inversion cancellation. -> Contracting canonical diagonal response.
- **step-error-contraction** [claim](#stmt-lem-rg-error-contraction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-rg-error-contraction): Even Gaussian guards, Taylor expansion, and spare support weights. -> Improved isolated-error contraction.
- **step-exact-rg** [claim](#stmt-thm-rg-step) / [proof](#subsec:rg-closure): Connected reassembly, finite Taylor extraction, and affine reset. -> Exact retained-class closure and comparison.
- **step-kinetic-increment** [claim](#stmt-lem-kinetic-increment) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-kinetic-increment): Finite-volume Laplace coefficient comparison before and after blocking. -> Identification of the limiting first kinetic increment.
- **step-shooting** [claim](#stmt-prop-shooting) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-shooting): Continuous shooting, disjoint barrier classes, and summable recursion errors. -> Admitted trajectories ending at the prescribed coupling.
- **step-endpoint-matching** [claim](#stmt-prop-endpoint-matching) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-endpoint-matching): Opposite-end iteration of shape and coupling discrepancies. -> Exponential endpoint density matching.
- **step-energy-remainder** [claim](#stmt-lem-comparison-remainder) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-comparison-remainder): Kernel truncation, support-hit estimates, and a small-cap lower bound. -> Local positive kinetic rows and controlled remainder.
- **step-row-moments** [claim](#stmt-lem-row-exponential-moment) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-row-exponential-moment): Chessboard dissemination and averaging over translated tilings. -> Selected-row exponential moments.
- **step-editable-regions** [claim](#stmt-lem-editable-regions) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-editable-regions): Exterior Lipschitz control, spherical filling, and cap sampling. -> Inventory-removing replacements with energy bounds.
- **step-integrated-comparison** [claim](#stmt-prop-integrated-comparison) / [proof](#pm-h-45): Exact inventory identities, integrated filling gain, and rooted forests. -> Integrated covering-activity comparison.
- **step-terminal-alignment** [claim](#stmt-cor-terminal-alignment) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-terminal-alignment): Reflection dissemination of a single-bond event. -> Rare endpoint misalignment.
- **step-reference-box** [claim](#stmt-prop-trace-small-box) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-trace-small-box): Balance preliminary mixing length against contracting coarse-volume error. -> A successful fixed physical reference box.
- **step-trace-concentration** [claim](#stmt-lem-trace-concentration) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-trace-concentration): Normalize positive transfer eigenvalue powers and square excited traces. -> Concentration and directional defect squaring.
- **step-rectangular-doubling** [claim](#stmt-prop-trace-doubling) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-trace-doubling): Combine coordinate-direction identities with defect squaring. -> Repeated-doubling decay and square-cylinder gap.
- **step-volume-slabs** [claim](#stmt-thm-trace-uniform) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-trace-uniform): Bounded insertion operators, ground-state projection, and telescoping volume doubling. -> Uniform volume comparison and bounded slab decay.
- **step-cutoff-gap** [claim](#stmt-cor-trace-physical-gap) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-trace-physical-gap): Positive spectral measures and density of centered local vectors. -> Full cutoff vacuum-complement spectral exclusion.
- **step-source-transport** [claim](#stmt-prop-source-step) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-source-step): Absolute source coefficients, isolated transfers, and bulk linear-response normalization. -> Exact source closure and contracting source comparison.
- **step-source-endpoints** [claim](#stmt-cor-source-endpoints) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-source-endpoints): Geometric convolution of source and background discrepancies. -> Fixed-bottom source convergence.
- **step-source-products** [claim](#stmt-prop-source-products) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-source-products): Clipped geometric comparison and summation of logarithmic response differences. -> Uniformly comparable normalization products.
- **step-moment-majorants** [claim](#stmt-prop-moment-majorants) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-moment-majorants): Positive monomial expansion and localized integrated source comparison. -> Factorial box bounds and local exponential moments.
- **step-shooting-limit** [claim](#stmt-prop-continuum-limit) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-continuum-limit): Coarse-cell approximation, moment determinacy, inclined matching, and characteristic-function volume comparison. -> Continuum laws and orientation comparison.
- **step-euclidean-regularity** [claim](#stmt-prop-euclidean-regularity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-euclidean-regularity): Weighted unit-box summation and dense irrational rotations. -> Tempered bounds and all Euclidean symmetries.
- **step-boundary-strips** [claim](#stmt-lem-boundary-strips) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-boundary-strips): Translation-invariant insertion counting and positive measure bounds. -> Indicator and moving-boundary convergence.
- **step-reflection-positivity** [claim](#stmt-lem-reflection-positivity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-reflection-positivity): Approximate the continuum reflection by microscopic seams and pass moments. -> Joint continuum reflection positivity.
- **step-polynomial-clustering** [claim](#stmt-prop-slab-clustering) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-slab-clustering): Exponential-tail truncation and bounded slab decay. -> A common clustering exponent for all field polynomials.
- **step-reconstruction** [claim](#stmt-prop-os-reconstruction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-os-reconstruction): Osterwalder–Schrader reconstruction with linear growth. -> Local relativistic Hermitian field theory.
- **step-continuum-gap** [claim](#stmt-prop-continuum-gap) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-continuum-gap): Remove equal-time surfaces in reflection norm, approximate ordered products, and exclude low spectral mass. -> Gap on the entire continuum vacuum complement.
- **step-non-gaussianity** [claim](#stmt-prop-non-gaussian) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-non-gaussian): Aligned cell moments, separated cumulant, and smooth boundary approximation. -> Nonzero separated connected correlation and nonzero vacuum complement.
- **step-main-theorem** [claim](#stmt-thm-main) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-non-gaussian-2): Assemble shooting, source limits, reconstruction, gap, and non-Gaussianity. -> The prescribed interacting massive continuum limit.
- **step-offset-rg-input** [claim](#stmt-prop-rg-input) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-rg-input): Deterministic canonical orbit and simultaneous bulk-period normalization. -> Canonical increments and common-tail comparison bounds.
- **step-kinetic-sensitivity** [claim](#stmt-lem-sensitivity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-sensitivity): Bulk raw-error comparison followed by the common affine extraction functional. -> Summable kinetic-error sensitivity.
- **step-offset-admission** [claim](#stmt-prop-admission) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-admission): First-exit contradiction and uniformly summable recursion errors. -> Strict admission for all prescribed types and depths.
- **step-retuning** [claim](#stmt-lem-retuning) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-retuning): Intermediate value theorem on the continuous terminal-coupling map. -> Exact terminal matching at arbitrary depth.
- **step-fixed-layer-matching** [claim](#stmt-prop-matching) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-matching): Boundary condition at large layers and coupled limsup supremum inequalities. -> Fixed-layer density and coupling convergence.
- **step-finite-beta** [claim](#stmt-lem-finite-beta) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-finite-beta): Mixing tails, positive monomial expansion, and incident-bond deletion. -> Positive finite susceptibility and length.
- **step-band-endpoints** [claim](#stmt-lem-band-endpoints) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-band-endpoints): Verify positivity and kinetic estimates uniformly throughout the terminal band. -> Band-uniform integrated comparison and alignment.
- **step-common-terminal-endpoints** [claim](#stmt-prop-endpoint-comparison) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-endpoint-comparison): Opposite-end discrepancy iteration and integrated gas comparison. -> Endpoint and logarithmic partition-function bounds.

      "depends_on": [
        "step-joint-integration",
        "step-canonical-contraction",

      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-thm-rg-step",
          "exact_quote": "Fix $\\upsilon>0$ sufficiently small. There are choices of $L$, the canonical caps and comparison weights, $P_0$, and finally $H$ such that integration against one normalized block observation sends every admitted retained density at $b\\in[H_j/2,2H_j]$ to an exact representation of the same form in layer $j-1$, with all renewed shape caps. The representation may be iterated when its new coupling belongs to $[H_{j-1}/2,2H_{j-1}]$; that admission is established separately by shooting in Section 5. Its precise coupling is $$b'=b+\\alpha_h(\\mathbf P)+\\frac{\\kappa_h(\\mathbf P)}b+\\Delta,\n \\qquad |\\Delta|\\le C_LH_j^{-1.05}.\n \\label{eq:orig-4}$$ Here $h$ is the free history, and the bulk scalar, canonical slots, and kicks use the prescriptions of Rloc@rg:canonical-mapRloc@rg:canonical-map**\\[unresolved R locator: rg:canonical-map\\]** adapted below to $S^2$. All retained norm caps are renewed.*\n\n\n*For two regular steps with common geometric scales, let $\\lambda=b_2-b_1$, and let $u$ be the fixed weighted shape discrepancy: canonical coefficient differences, regular-error difference divided by its cap, and covering-gas difference divided by its cap. The regular error difference is measured through order $k-1$. Then $$\\begin{aligned}\n u'&\\le q u+C_L\\operatorname{poly}(H_j)\\epsilon_h\n       +C_L(\\log H_j)^C|\\lambda|/H_j,\\nonumber\\\\\n |\\lambda'-\\lambda|&\\le C_Lu+C_L\\operatorname{poly}(H_j)\\epsilon_h\n       +C_L(\\log H_j)^C|\\lambda|/H_j,\n \\qquad q<L^{-2+\\upsilon}.\n \\label{eq:orig-5}\n\\end{aligned}$$ For identical histories $\\epsilon_h=0$. If the histories share their last $r$ regular observations, one may take $\\epsilon_h=(A_0/L^2)^r$, with the constant $A_0$ of Section 3. The same-step Lipschitz bounds with no history change hold also for an inclined first step. The representation classes and constants are common to all the admitted histories and periods. Signed covering activities are allowed: the logarithm used in constructing the regular exponent is the convergent connected logarithm of the small background factor, based at one. The mandatory-cover factor is retained as a sum, and no logarithm of the full signed density is taken.",
          "source_id": "PM-215.1"
        }
      ],

Every such choice satisfies $$\\beta_N=H+\\gamma N+O_{L,H}(\\log(2+N)).\n \\label{eq:orig-12}$$ Along these trajectories, $$b_j=\\vartheta_j+O_L(1),\\qquad 0\\le j\\le N,\n \\label{eq:orig-13}$$ uniformly in $N$, with constants bounded as $H$ is increased. The trajectories starting at the same $\\beta_N$ with either inclined first step are also strictly admitted and satisfy Equation <a href=\"#eq:orig-13\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:orig-13\">[eq:orig-13]</a>.           "exact_quote": "Consider an admitted source-free step of Section 4 from layer $j$ to layer $j-1$, with precise coupling $b\\in[H_j/2,2H_j]$, together with source lists satisfying Equation <a href=\"#eq:orig-27\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:orig-27\">[eq:orig-27]</a> and the normalization and support conditions above.           "exact_quote": "For every $n\\ge1$ and every component array $\\boldsymbol\\alpha$, the measure $S_{n,N}^{\\boldsymbol\\alpha}$ is nonnegative. The same bound holds in the periodic infinite-plane state.*\n\n\n*For each fixed number $D$ of terminal cells, their component field sums have joint exponential moments in a neighborhood of the origin, uniformly in these cutoffs and axis tori.       "evidence": [

          "anchor": "stmt-thm-main",
          "exact_quote": "There are a dyadic integer $L>1$, a constant $H>0$, bare couplings $\\beta_N\\to\\infty$, and field normalizations $B_N>0$, such that $$\\label{eq:main-prescription}\n a_N=L^{-N},\\qquad\n \\beta_N=H+\\frac{\\log L}{2\\pi}N+O(\\log(N+1)),$$ and the following assertions hold for the model <a href=\"#eq:lattice-model\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:lattice-model\">[eq:lattice-model]</a>.*\n\n1.  *Every finite list of the variables $\\phi_N(f)=\\phi_{a_N,B_N}(f)$, under $\\mu_{\\beta_N}$, converges jointly in law and in all moments. The component Schwinger distributions converge in $\\mathcal S'((\\mathbb R^2)^n)$ at every order. They reconstruct a local, unitary, relativistic theory in $1+1$ dimensions.*\n\n3.  *The reconstructed theory has a unique vacuum $\\Omega$, a nonzero vacuum complement, and a Hamiltonian $H_{\\mathrm{phys}}$ satisfying $$H_{\\mathrm{phys}}\\big|_{\\Omega^\\perp}\\ge m\\mathbf 1\n     \\quad\\text{for some }m>0.$$*\n\n4.  *A connected four-point distribution is nonzero on smooth tests with strictly separated time supports.           "anchor": "stmt-prop-rg-input",
          "exact_quote": "For every type $P\\in\\{r,+,-\\}$, initialize the nearest-neighbor model as in Section 5.       "evidence": [

<a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **invariant-canonical-continuum-limit**: For the specified nearest-neighbor model and periodic thermodynamic state, susceptibility and second-moment length normalization give a common limiting hierarchy through all diverging real bare couplings. Convergence includes joint laws, joint moments, and strong convergence of component Schwinger distributions.
- **invariant-gap-on-entire-vacuum-complement**: The reconstructed Hamiltonian has a strictly positive lower bound on the entire vacuum complement. The complement is nonzero, and its spectral bottom is finite.
- **invariant-separated-non-wick-correlations**: A connected four-point distribution survives on smooth tests with strictly separated ordered time supports. The limiting field correlations therefore fail Wick factorization.
- **invariant-normalization-requires-positive-global-moments**: Canonical normalization uses finite positive susceptibility and finite positive second-moment length. Uniform two-point tails permit convergence of the full relative mass and second moment, and the resulting positive constant length and field rescaling is unique.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-use-modified-microscopic-action**: Apply the canonical continuum conclusion to models with an external field, a topological term, or another lattice action. -> The canonical convergence assertion concerns the specified nearest-neighbor action and periodic thermodynamic state; it supplies no comparison theorem for those modified models.
- **anti-use-target-dimension-transfer**: Reuse a mass theorem for another target dimension as the proof of the present continuum construction. -> Changing the target dimension changes the current identities, Gaussian normalization, and coupling drift.
- **anti-use-gaussian-continuum-surrogate**: Replace the limiting hierarchy by a Gaussian field and compute all higher correlations by Wick factorization. -> The separated connected four-point distribution is nonzero, so this replacement removes an established property of the limiting field.
- **anti-use-pointwise-correlations**: Treat the correlation measures as pointwise functions or assume an equal-time product prescription. -> Distributional convergence and smeared reconstruction do not supply pointwise fields or arbitrary equal-time products.
- **anti-use-local-convergence-for-global-normalization**: Infer convergence of susceptibility and second-moment length solely from convergence on compact tests. -> Local convergence alone does not control relative two-point mass escaping to large separations.
- **anti-use-signed-cover-as-probability**: Take the logarithm of the full signed covering density or use a restricted signed covering sum as a probability normalizer. -> The representation permits signed activities, while the comparison and reflection arguments require positivity of the complete actual base law.
- **anti-use-finite-check-as-continuum-certificate**: Use agreement on finitely many lattice configurations or transfer spectra to certify the full continuum theorem. -> The principal assertions require cutoff removal, thermodynamic limits, convergence at every order, and spectral exclusion on a Hilbert-space closure.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `not_applicable`. The engineering target is the canonical continuum hierarchy and its reconstructed interacting massive theory, rather than a finite constructive subidentity. Theorem 1 states: "The following limits hold through all real values of $\beta$ tending to infinity." Proposition 41 concerns the Hamiltonian on the entire vacuum complement; its proof extends spectral exclusion by density and bounded spectral projections. Finite enumeration, finite transfer approximations, or checks of the block geometry cannot decide those continuum and Hilbert-space assertions. A finite executable oracle would therefore cover only a restricted auxiliary identity and would not certify this target.

## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **limit-specified-microscopic-action** (hypothesis): The canonical limit concerns the specified nearest-neighbor sphere-valued spin action without an external field or a topological term. Blocked use: ['Apply the continuum conclusion to an action with an external field or a topological term.', 'Infer universality across different microscopic interactions from canonical normalization alone.']
- **limit-periodic-state-prescription** (hypothesis): The thermodynamic state is selected by the periodic square-torus prescription. The asserted uniqueness of that periodic limit does not by itself classify every possible infinite-volume Gibbs state. Blocked use: ['Replace the periodic thermodynamic state by an arbitrary boundary-selected state without a comparison argument.']
- **limit-target-dimension-adaptation** (formal_scope): Current identities, Gaussian normalization, and coupling drift depend on the target dimension. The adaptation of intermediate estimates does not transfer another target's mass theorem. Blocked use: ['Reuse the coupling drift or continuum spectral conclusion for a different spin target without deriving the corresponding estimates.']
- **limit-preliminary-mixing-regime** (hypothesis): The preliminary mixing estimate requires its strength ceiling and sufficiently large scale. Its torus assertion concerns unpinned rectangular tori with the stated side bounds, while its other geometric class consists of finite free subgraphs. Blocked use: ['Apply the preliminary covariance bound to arbitrary pinned tori or to rectangles below its side threshold.', 'Treat the preliminary exponential length as an exact correlation-length asymptotic.']
- **limit-stiffness-iteration-size-premise** (hypothesis): Stiffness iteration requires a uniform pinned-cell bound and the auxiliary size restriction throughout the iteration, including every proposed enlargement. Blocked use: ['Continue the stiffness iteration after checking its size premise only on the initial square.', 'Use a stiffness bound established for selected boundary pins as the uniform input.']
- **limit-block-mean-branches** (edge_case): The unit-mean observation includes a measurable fallback branch. The stronger quadratic mean-error estimate forces the normalized branch only under the prescribed within-cell chord bounds and sufficiently large terminal coupling. Blocked use: ['Differentiate the fallback prescription as though it were globally smooth.', 'Apply the quadratic mean-error bound to arbitrary rough spin configurations.']
- **limit-free-history-comparison** (hypothesis): History contraction compares identified output coordinates and a common tail of ordinary observations using the same averaging map. Its analytic and kernel norms are those specified for the free operators. Blocked use: ['Infer history contraction for unrelated observation tails or unidentified coordinate frames.', 'Interpret the scalar Gaussian precision update as the complete nonlinear spin transformation.']
- **limit-complete-records-and-periods** (hypothesis): Locality uses complete dependencies, including mask reads, eligibility tests, absence tests, and joining paths. Finite periods must be compatible with all applied blockings, and winding calculations retain their separate record prices. Blocked use: ['Declare factors independent because their displayed spin arguments are disjoint while their complete supports overlap.', 'Discard a winding charge because its final displayed expression has small support.', 'Apply periodized formulas on a quotient incompatible with a blocking.']
- **limit-exact-step-admission-and-parameter-order** (hypothesis): Retained-class closure assumes the full admission conditions and the prescribed order of parameter choices. Renewing shape caps does not alone prove that the next precise coupling lies in its required band. Blocked use: ['Iterate the exact step solely because its shape caps were renewed.', 'Change geometric reference thresholds with the precise coupling during a comparison.', 'Treat the formal canonical coefficient map as the entire exact integral.']
- **limit-ambient-completion-and-prediction-domains** (hypothesis): Ambient completion fixes the pattern, frozen variables, tags, and output statuses. The sharpened prediction estimates apply on protected stencils in the empty pattern or away from nearby cores; extensions near cores have only the stated global mean bound. Blocked use: ['Treat the auxiliary normal Gaussian as an added physical field.', 'Apply the suppressed-gradient prediction to unprotected core rows.', 'Differentiate discontinuous output statuses across their jumps.']
- **limit-product-estimates-and-error-normalization** (hypothesis): Joint estimates concern admissible prepared factors with compulsory cores and their reserves retained. Improved error contraction uses the normalized invariant error class, including removal of the affine Hessian and the specified derivative budget. Blocked use: ['Factor overlapping Gaussian reads into independent expectations.', 'Drop exceptional reserves before estimating products or derivatives.', 'Transfer the improved error contraction to an arbitrary unnormalized local function.']
- **limit-shooting-and-retuning-effectivity** (nonconstructive): Shooting and retuning select couplings by continuity and existence arguments. Retuning does not establish monotonicity or uniqueness of the terminal-coupling map. Blocked use: ['Assume a unique microscopic shooting value.', 'Use a monotone root-search contract or a calibrated stopping tolerance without additional estimates.']
- **limit-signed-covers-and-positive-base-law** (hypothesis): Signed covering activities are permitted, but mandatory inventories remain exact. Integrated comparison requires a complete positive and reflection-positive base density under the stated axis-torus and activity-cap hypotheses. Blocked use: ['Take the logarithm of the full signed covering density.', 'Normalize by a restricted signed covering sum.', 'Apply the integrated comparison to an arbitrary signed base law or to an inclined endpoint without establishing its required positivity properties.']
- **limit-reference-box-and-transfer-smallness** (hypothesis): The transfer conclusion is conditional on a sufficiently small rectangular doubling defect and the stated positive-transfer geometry. The existence of a successful physical reference box depends on the preceding analytic comparisons. Blocked use: ['Infer a spectral ratio bound from an arbitrary finite-volume partition-function calculation.', 'Omit the reference-box smallness test, minimum periods, or auxiliary aspect requirements.', 'Treat an existential reference-box choice as a supplied numerical tolerance.']
- **limit-source-transport-prescriptions** (hypothesis): Field normalization follows exact source transport with positive bulk response coefficients. Source records retain their support and degree information, and source-dependent constants are not removed as volume scalars. Blocked use: ['Replace the accumulated source normalization by an independently chosen factor without matching the resulting fields.', 'Discard supported spin-independent higher source terms when computing moments.', 'Use a discrepancy on an isolated finite torus to determine the bulk response coefficient.']
- **limit-fixed-layer-and-fixed-torus-convergence** (hypothesis): Matched source and density comparisons are established at each fixed bottom layer and on fixed compatible periods. Inclined moment bounds may depend on the fixed physical torus. Blocked use: ['Promote fixed-layer convergence to a uniform estimate over growing layers without an additional bound.', 'Assume inclined moment constants are uniform over an increasing physical volume.', 'Exchange cutoff and volume limits using unbounded observables without the moment or characteristic-function arguments.']
- **limit-distributional-fields-and-boundary-approximations** (formal_scope): The correlations are measures and tempered distributions tested by smearings. Reconstruction supplies neither pointwise Euclidean fields nor an unrestricted equal-time product prescription; indicator approximations use the boundary estimates. Blocked use: ['Evaluate a general Schwinger distribution as a pointwise correlation function.', 'Insert arbitrary equal-time products without establishing their meaning.', 'Extend box-indicator convergence to unrestricted measurable sets solely from compact continuous-test convergence.']
- **limit-global-normalization-needs-tails-and-positivity** (hypothesis): Susceptibility and second-moment normalization require convergence of the full relative two-point mass and second moment, with finite strictly positive limiting quantities. Compact-test convergence alone does not establish these conditions. Blocked use: ['Normalize using truncated correlations without controlling the omitted tails.', 'Infer positive second-moment length solely from a coincident-point lower bound.', 'Apply the positive rescaling when susceptibility or length vanishes or is not finite.']
- **limit-offset-matching-and-dense-period-hypotheses** (hypothesis): Fixed-layer matching uses transient-corrected offsets, diverging depths, and common ordinary bottom observations. Offset independence additionally requires continuous hierarchy evaluations, a continuous positive length, both scale relations, the specified rotations, and sufficient interval overlap. Blocked use: ['Identify unnormalized offset hierarchies merely because their bare offsets are close.', 'Infer offset independence from a single scale relation.', 'Replace continuity or positive length by an unsupported finite sample of offsets.']
- **limit-full-gap-reconstruction-and-density** (formal_scope): The full Hamiltonian gap concerns the reconstructed theory and follows from a common polynomial clustering exponent together with density and positive spectral measures. A spin two-point estimate alone is insufficient for that full-space conclusion. Blocked use: ['Infer a gap on every reconstructed state from decay of only the spin two-point function.', 'Treat a finite transfer approximation as a certificate for the entire continuum vacuum complement.', 'Infer an isolated particle pole or an exact spectral mass from the positive lower bound alone.']
- **limit-separated-non-gaussianity-scope** (counterexample_scope): Non-Gaussianity is witnessed by the existence of a nonzero connected correlation on suitably chosen smooth tests with separated ordered time supports. It is not a claim that every such choice has a nonzero connected correlation. Blocked use: ['Assume every separated test configuration has a nonzero connected correlation.', 'Replace the limiting hierarchy by Wick factorization.']
- **limit-uncalibrated-continuum-constants** (unknown): Explicit numerical choices sufficient for every large-parameter condition and a numerical value of the continuum spectral bottom are ABSENT from the supplied construction. Blocked use: ['Use the existence assertions as calibrated simulation parameters or certified numerical convergence tolerances.', 'Report an exact continuum mass from the existence of a positive Hamiltonian lower bound.']

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


We construct a canonical interacting massive continuum limit of the two-dimensional nearest-neighbor $`O(3)`$ model with unit-length spins, no external field, and no topological term. Normalized by susceptibility and second-moment correlation length, the limit exists as the bare coupling tends to infinity through all positive real values, without selecting subsequences. The limiting fields satisfy the Osterwalder–Schrader axioms and have a nonzero connected four-point correlation on separated time supports. Their reconstructed theory has a unique vacuum, a nonzero vacuum complement, and a positive Hamiltonian gap on that entire complement.

<a id="sec:introduction"></a>
##### Introduction

<a id="eq:lattice-model"></a>
The two-dimensional nonlinear sigma model asks how a field constrained to a curved compact target can produce a relativistic quantum field theory at distances much larger than a lattice spacing. For the sphere $S^2$, the basic lattice model has a particularly simple definition. On a finite periodic square lattice $\Lambda$, let $q_x\in S^2\subset\mathbb R^3$ and let $\sigma$ be normalized area measure on $S^2$. Its Gibbs probability is $$\label{eq:lattice-model}
 \,\mathrm d\mu_{\beta,\Lambda}(q)
 =\frac{1}{Z_{\beta,\Lambda}}
   \exp\!\left(\beta\sum_{\{x,y\}\in E(\Lambda)}q_x\cdot q_y\right)
   \prod_{x\in\Lambda}\,\mathrm d\sigma(q_x),
 \qquad \beta>0,$$ where each nearest-neighbor bond occurs once. We consider no topological term and no external field. The continuum problem is to let the coupling $\beta$ diverge and the lattice spacing vanish while preserving a nontrivial physical scale. A mass estimate at fixed lattice spacing does not settle this problem: one must construct the same limiting fields on which the limiting gap acts.

<a id="subsec:history"></a>
###### Historical context

The nonordering theorem of Mermin and Wagner, and Mermin’s classical version, exclude spontaneous magnetization in the corresponding finite-range two-dimensional systems (Mermin and Wagner 1966; Mermin 1967) <a id="pm-cite-1"></a>[[MW](#ref-MW), [Mermin1967](#ref-Mermin1967)]. McBryan and Spencer obtained algebraic upper bounds on spin correlations by complex rotations (McBryan and Spencer 1977) <a id="pm-cite-2"></a>[[McBryanSpencer](#ref-McBryanSpencer)]. Such an upper bound does not distinguish algebraic decay from exponential decay. Local Ward identities gave further correlation inequalities and high-temperature mass-gap criteria in the work of Aizenman and Simon (Aizenman and Simon 1980) <a id="pm-cite-3"></a>[[AizenmanSimonWard](#ref-AizenmanSimonWard)]. A continuum mass theorem additionally requires control as the bare inverse coupling diverges and the lattice spacing vanishes.

For more than two spin components, perturbative renormalization predicts that weak microscopic coupling produces an exponentially large correlation length. Polyakov identified the renormalization-group mechanism for two-dimensional Goldstone fields (Polyakov 1975) <a id="pm-cite-4"></a>[[Polyakov](#ref-Polyakov)]. Brézin and Zinn-Justin developed the expansion near two dimensions, and Brézin, Zinn-Justin and Le Guillou analyzed the renormalization of the model and its composite operators (Brézin and Zinn-Justin 1976; Brézin, Zinn-Justin, and Le Guillou 1976) <a id="pm-cite-5"></a>[[BrezinZinnJustin](#ref-BrezinZinnJustin), [BrezinZinnJustinLeGuillou](#ref-BrezinZinnJustinLeGuillou)]. These works explain why weak microscopic coupling can coexist with a finite long-distance mass scale. They also identify the perturbative coefficients against which a constructive renormalization should be checked. Establishing those coefficients is logically different from bounding the nonperturbative remainder throughout a trajectory whose length diverges with the cutoff.

Integrability gives a complementary and much more detailed picture of the expected continuum theory. Zamolodchikov and Zamolodchikov solved the factorization, crossing and unitarity equations for $O(N)$-invariant scattering and identified the sigma-model solution (Zamolodchikov and Zamolodchikov 1979) <a id="pm-cite-6"></a>[[ZamolodchikovZamolodchikov](#ref-ZamolodchikovZamolodchikov)]. Hasenfratz, Maggiore and Niedermayer obtained the exact mass-to-renormalization-scale relation for $O(3)$ and $O(4)$ by matching the Bethe ansatz with perturbation theory (Hasenfratz, Maggiore, and Niedermayer 1990) <a id="pm-cite-7"></a>[[HasenfratzMaggioreNiedermayer](#ref-HasenfratzMaggioreNiedermayer)]; Hasenfratz and Niedermayer extended the calculation to arbitrary $N\ge3$ (Hasenfratz and Niedermayer 1990) <a id="pm-cite-8"></a>[[HasenfratzNiedermayer](#ref-HasenfratzNiedermayer)]. Those calculations determine a mass ratio within the integrable continuum description. The additional problem addressed here is to construct the field distributions from the specified nearest-neighbor measure and to establish their spectral properties after removal of the cutoff. No factorized scattering matrix is used as a premise of the construction.

Susceptibility and second-moment correlation length provide intrinsic field and length units. This is the familiar zero-momentum normalization, used explicitly by Campostrini, Pelissetto, Rossi and Vicari (Campostrini et al. 1997) <a id="pm-cite-9"></a>[[CampostriniPelissettoRossiVicari1997](#ref-CampostriniPelissettoRossiVicari1997)]. Their strong-coupling calculations and the lattice–bootstrap comparisons of Balog and collaborators (Balog et al. 1999) <a id="pm-cite-10"></a>[[BalogEtAl1999](#ref-BalogEtAl1999)] studied normalized amplitudes and supplied evidence for continuum universality. Here the question is convergence of the entire canonically normalized Schwinger hierarchy for the specified nearest-neighbor model and periodic thermodynamic state, as the bare coupling tends to infinity without restriction to a selected sequence. Comparing this limit with a terminal-coupling construction requires control of both the field distributions and the normalizing correlation moments.

Rigorous work has supplied several distinct parts of this program. Kupiainen proved asymptotic validity of the $1/N$ expansion for lattice models above the spherical-model critical temperature and obtained a mass gap for sufficiently large $N$ at each such temperature (Kupiainen 1980) <a id="pm-cite-11"></a>[[Kupiainen](#ref-Kupiainen)]. Kopper later proved mass generation at sufficiently large finite $N$ with a suitable ultraviolet cutoff (Kopper 1999) <a id="pm-cite-12"></a>[[Kopper](#ref-Kopper)]. These large-$N$ results do not specialize to a cutoff-removed construction at $N=3$. Gawędzki and Kupiainen constructed a continuum limit with asymptotic freedom for a sigma model with a *hierarchical* kinetic term (Gawędzki and Kupiainen 1986) <a id="pm-cite-13"></a>[[GawedzkiKupiainen](#ref-GawedzkiKupiainen)]. In that setting the hierarchical covariance reduces the flow to a single-spin recursion. For the nearest-neighbor model, integration generates interactions between blocks whose spatial decay must be controlled. Mitter and Ramadas constructed the Wilson renormalized trajectory in perturbation theory in the effective charge and developed the corresponding effective-action analysis (Mitter and Ramadas 1989) <a id="pm-cite-14"></a>[[MitterRamadas](#ref-MitterRamadas)].

The organization by successive block integrations belongs to the renormalization-group tradition of Kadanoff and Wilson (Kadanoff 1966; Wilson 1971) <a id="pm-cite-15"></a>[[Kadanoff](#ref-Kadanoff), [Wilson](#ref-Wilson)]. Bałaban developed localized effective actions and constrained variational methods in lattice gauge theory (Bałaban 1987, 1985) <a id="pm-cite-16"></a>[[BalabanGaugeFlow](#ref-BalabanGaugeFlow), [BalabanGaugeVariational](#ref-BalabanGaugeVariational)] and in the low-temperature analysis of classical $N$-vector models (Bałaban 1995, 1996) <a id="pm-cite-17"></a>[[BalabanFlow](#ref-BalabanFlow), [BalabanVariational](#ref-BalabanVariational)]. Goswami studied the constrained background-field problem for two-dimensional $SU(n)$ chiral models, including the $O(4)$ case (Goswami 2024) <a id="pm-cite-18"></a>[[Goswami2024](#ref-Goswami2024)]. For the two-dimensional $O(4)$ model, Dybalski, Stottmeister and Tanimoto proved existence and uniqueness for the constrained small-field variational problem associated with one block-averaging operation (Dybalski, Stottmeister, and Tanimoto 2024) <a id="pm-cite-19"></a>[[DybalskiStottmeisterTanimotoVariational](#ref-DybalskiStottmeisterTanimotoVariational)]. Aru, Garban and Sepúlveda proved that, after fixing one spin direction, rescaled transverse fluctuations converge locally as the inverse coupling tends to infinity to a rooted vector-valued lattice Gaussian free field (Aru, Garban, and Sepúlveda 2025, Theorem 1.3) <a id="pm-cite-20"></a>[[AGS](#ref-AGS)]. For $O(3)$ this field has two components. Their result identifies the local Gaussian approximation; the construction below also requires control at spatial scales that grow with the inverse coupling.

<a id="pm-h-4"></a>
###### Canonical normalization and the main result

For each $\beta$ used below, write $\mu_\beta$ for the local limit of periodic square tori as their side lengths tend to infinity. Existence and uniqueness of this periodic limit are part of the preliminary estimates. Given a lattice spacing $a>0$, a positive field normalization $B$, and $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$, define the three-component random variable $$\phi_{a,B}(f)=Ba^2\sum_{x\in\mathbb Z^2}f(ax)q_x.$$ For component indices $i_1,\ldots,i_n\in\{1,2,3\}$, the corresponding Schwinger distribution is the expectation of the product of these smeared fields. Its extension to general tests on $(\mathbb R^2)^n$ is equivalently the discrete moment measure with weight $(Ba^2)^n$.

<a id="eq:canonical-lattice-scales"></a>
<a id="eq:canonical-field"></a>
The lattice itself supplies two normalization constants. Put $$\label{eq:canonical-lattice-scales}
 C_\beta(x)=\mathbb E_{\mu_\beta}[q_0^1q_x^1],\qquad
 \chi_\beta=\sum_{x\in\mathbb Z^2}C_\beta(x),\qquad
 \xi_\beta^2=\frac{1}{4\chi_\beta}
                 \sum_{x\in\mathbb Z^2}|x|^2 C_\beta(x).$$ Here $\chi_\beta$ is the susceptibility of one spin component, and $\xi_\beta$ is the positive second-moment correlation length. For a vector test $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb R^3)$ define $$\label{eq:canonical-field}
 \Psi_\beta(f)=\frac{1}{\xi_\beta\sqrt{\chi_\beta}}
           \sum_{x\in\mathbb Z^2} f(x/\xi_\beta)\cdot q_x.$$ The factor $4$ in <a href="#eq:canonical-lattice-scales" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:canonical-lattice-scales">[eq:canonical-lattice-scales]</a> is twice the Euclidean dimension. For a translation-invariant continuum two-point measure written in relative coordinates as $\,\mathrm dy\,\nu(\,\mathrm dz)$, with $z=y_2-y_1$, its susceptibility and squared second-moment length are $\nu(\mathbb R^2)$ and $\int|z|^2\nu(\,\mathrm dz)/(4\nu(\mathbb R^2))$, respectively, whenever these quantities are finite and positive.

<a id="stmt-thm-canonical"></a>
<div id="thm:canonical" class="theorem">

**Theorem 1** (Canonical continuum limit). *For the nearest-neighbor probability <a href="#eq:lattice-model" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:lattice-model">[eq:lattice-model]</a>, the periodic thermodynamic limit $\mu_\beta$ exists for all sufficiently large $\beta$. Both sums in <a href="#eq:canonical-lattice-scales" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:canonical-lattice-scales">[eq:canonical-lattice-scales]</a> are finite, $\chi_\beta,\xi_\beta>0$, and $\xi_\beta\to\infty$ as $\beta\to\infty$. The following limits hold through all real values of $\beta$ tending to infinity.*

1.  *For every finite list of vector tests in $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb R^3)$, the fields <a href="#eq:canonical-field" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:canonical-field">[eq:canonical-field]</a> converge jointly in law and in all joint moments to one common limiting hierarchy.*

2.  *For every order and every choice of spin components, the associated Schwinger distributions converge in the strong topology of $\mathcal S'((\mathbb R^2)^n)$, that is, uniformly on bounded sets of Schwartz tests.*

3.  *The limiting hierarchy has susceptibility and second-moment length equal to one. It is the hierarchy constructed in Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">2</a>, after the unique positive constant length and field rescalings imposing these two normalizations.*

</div>

The assertion concerns the one lattice action and periodic thermodynamic state specified above. The normalization removes the freedom to choose constant physical length and field units. It does not introduce a comparison with other lattice actions, external fields, or topological terms.

<a id="pm-h-5"></a>
###### Construction and physical properties

The proof first constructs the fields at a prescribed physical block scale. This gives the following more detailed existence statement, including the physical properties that will pass to the canonical limit.

<a id="stmt-thm-main"></a>
<div id="thm:main" class="theorem">

**Theorem 2**. *There are a dyadic integer $L>1$, a constant $H>0$, bare couplings $\beta_N\to\infty$, and field normalizations $B_N>0$, such that <a id="eq:main-prescription"></a>$$\label{eq:main-prescription}
 a_N=L^{-N},\qquad
 \beta_N=H+\frac{\log L}{2\pi}N+O(\log(N+1)),$$ and the following assertions hold for the model <a href="#eq:lattice-model" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:lattice-model">[eq:lattice-model]</a>.*

1.  *Every finite list of the variables $\phi_N(f)=\phi_{a_N,B_N}(f)$, under $\mu_{\beta_N}$, converges jointly in law and in all moments. The component Schwinger distributions converge in $\mathcal S'((\mathbb R^2)^n)$ at every order. The same limits are obtained with suitable periodic physical tori tending to the plane as $N\to\infty$.*

2.  *The limiting Schwinger distributions are Euclidean invariant, internally $O(3)$ invariant, reflection positive, symmetric and clustering. For every component distribution and $F\in\mathcal S((\mathbb R^2)^n)$, $$|S_n(F)|\le C^n n!\sup_{x\in(\mathbb R^2)^n}
           (1+|x|^2)^{2n}|F(x)|,$$ with a constant $C$ independent of $n$. They reconstruct a local, unitary, relativistic theory in $1+1$ dimensions.*

3.  *The reconstructed theory has a unique vacuum $\Omega$, a nonzero vacuum complement, and a Hamiltonian $H_{\mathrm{phys}}$ satisfying $$H_{\mathrm{phys}}\big|_{\Omega^\perp}\ge m\mathbf 1
     \quad\text{for some }m>0.$$*

4.  *A connected four-point distribution is nonzero on smooth tests with strictly separated time supports. In particular, the limiting field correlations do not satisfy Wick factorization.*

*The trajectory is selected by fixing its terminal kinetic coupling to $H$ at a fixed physical block length.*

</div>

Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">2</a> constructs a continuum limit along a prescribed trajectory. Theorem <a href="#thm:canonical" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:canonical">1</a> identifies its canonical normalization with the limit along every diverging bare coupling. Interaction is expressed by the fourth assertion of Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">2</a>: a connected four-point correlation of the constructed field is nonzero. The mass-gap estimate and this criterion use the same fields and the same choice of physical units.

<a id="stmt-cor-canonical-physics"></a>
<div id="cor:canonical-physics" class="corollary">

**Corollary 3**. *The canonical limiting hierarchy is Euclidean invariant, internally $O(3)$ invariant, reflection positive, symmetric, and clustering. It satisfies factorial tempered-distribution bounds and reconstructs a local, unitary relativistic theory in $1+1$ dimensions. The reconstructed Hamiltonian has a unique vacuum, a nonzero vacuum complement, and a strictly positive lower bound on that entire complement. A connected four-point distribution is nonzero on smooth tests with strictly separated time supports.*

</div>

<a id="pm-h-6"></a>
###### Proof strategy and new estimates

The starting analytic tools are the local angular-integration and exact blocking constructions in (OpenAI 2026) <a id="pm-cite-21"></a>[[OpenAI-O4](#ref-OpenAI-O4)], denoted by R when discussing their adaptation. We use their stated intermediate estimates with the hypotheses specified below. We do not transfer the $O(4)$ mass theorem to $O(3)$. The difference in target dimension changes the current identities, the Gaussian normalization and the coefficient of the coupling drift. Sections <a href="#sec:preliminary" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:preliminary">1</a> and 4 establish these changes directly. Section <a href="#sec:setup" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:setup">2</a> fixes the imported definitions and identifies the dimension-independent inputs.

An exact blocking partitions the lattice into squares, introduces one retained spin in $S^2$ per square through a normalized averaging kernel, and integrates the fine spins. This preserves the partition function and, when sources are retained, the generating function of the original spins. One carries those sources and all the corrections they generate through successive integrations. At a step with side factor $l$, rescale the source at each fine site in a block to $l^{-2}$ times its retained source $z$. On a constant retained-spin configuration $V$, the resulting linear term is $c_{j,N}z\cdot V$. Normalize its coefficient to one. Section 8 constructs these positive coefficients and proves that the accumulated field normalization is $B_N=\prod_{j=1}^N c_{j,N}^{-1}$.

The proof must connect a rough large-distance estimate with a precise comparison at a fixed physical scale. Four additional estimates make that connection possible.

First, write $X(\beta)=C\exp((4\pi-\eta)\beta)$ for a preliminary upper bound on the mixing length, where $\eta>0$ is fixed. The strict saving below $4\pi$ comes from the transverse fluctuations in the first coarse tile. The pinned-cell inputs are uniform over boundary pins. The resulting mixing estimate is uniform under cuts and weaker bonds.

Second, spatial inversion and tangent reflection give contraction of the terms remaining after extraction of the kinetic coupling and its specified low-order corrections. The contraction can be made arbitrarily close to $L^{-2}$ per step. The affine quadratic contribution has already been removed by the kinetic normalization; inversion cancels the next spatial cross term. This additional cancellation allows the coarse comparison box to grow while the total error in its density still tends to zero.

Third, an integrated comparison controls changes in the gas of large-gradient regions. We fill selected regions with small-gradient spins, retain the complete positive density at the filled configuration, and pay the filling entropy with the original gradient energy. The comparison loses only a volume factor. The strict saving in the preliminary length permits a reference box larger than that mixing length, while the nearly $L^{-2}$ contraction keeps the error over its coarse volume small. Together these estimates transfer a finite-box criterion for exponential decay from one reference cutoff to every finer cutoff at one fixed physical box. The transfer-operator criterion then gives a common physical decay rate. More concretely, at a reference depth $K$, the preliminary mixing length in physical units is $$a_KX(\beta_K)=L^{(1-\eta/(2\pi))K+o(K)}.$$ Matching the effective densities to finer cutoffs is controlled by the error parameter $C_H M^2L^{-(2-\upsilon)K}$ in a physical square of side $M$, where $\upsilon>0$ can be chosen arbitrarily small. Thus $M$ can be much larger than the mixing length while this error tends to zero. Fixing one sufficiently large $K$ fixes a successful physical square once and for all; its decay criterion passes to every finer cutoff.

Fourth, independent local sources are carried through the exact transformation. Their linear response defines $B_N$; the remaining source terms contract. This gives convergence of the actual smeared lattice spins, local exponential moments, and a fourth cumulant that survives the limit. Two reflected inclined first blockings compare regulator orientations through a common coarse frame. The resulting rotation has angle equal to an irrational multiple of $\pi$. Together with continuity, it gives full Euclidean rotation invariance.

The resulting architecture separates the long-distance estimate from the source construction. Sections 3–5 construct and match the exact trajectories. Sections 6–7 obtain the estimate uniform in the cutoff. Sections 8–9 construct the Schwinger distributions and prove their symmetries. Section 10 reconstructs the quantum theory and proves both the full spectral gap and non-Wick factorization.

The final step is to make the physical normalization intrinsic to the lattice. An arbitrary large bare coupling can be written as a reference coupling at an integer depth plus a bounded real offset. The effective hierarchy initially may depend on that offset. A summable sensitivity estimate for the noncanonical kinetic increment, proved in Lemma <a href="#lem:sensitivity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:sensitivity">44</a>, shows that trajectories with the same corrected offset agree at each fixed coarse scale. This is stronger than a bound on the size of the increment: it controls its change under perturbations of the trajectory. The resulting argument in Section <a href="#sec:trajectories" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:trajectories">1</a> is useful whenever a marginal coupling must be matched over arbitrarily many renormalization steps.

Section <a href="#sec:volume" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:volume">2</a> extends the fixed-scale volume comparison to these bounded offsets. Section 3 then constructs their continuum hierarchies and proves uniform two-point tails. The tails permit passage of the full susceptibility and second moment to the limit, so the normalization in <a href="#eq:canonical-field" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:canonical-field">[eq:canonical-field]</a> can be applied after taking the continuum limit. Finally, Section 4 compares two descriptions of the same microscopic field: adjacent ordinary depths, and an ordinary versus an inclined first blocking. Besides rotating the lattice, the inclined step contributes a length factor $5$, multiplicatively independent of the dyadic factor $L$. The two reflected inclinations remove the rotation; continuity and the two resulting incommensurable offset periods remove the remaining offset dependence. Thus the same exact blocking geometry serves both Euclidean symmetry and canonical uniqueness.

The conditional comparisons in the preliminary mixing argument use Ginibre’s formulation of ferromagnetic correlation inequalities and the positive-association theorem of Fortuin, Kasteleyn and Ginibre (Ginibre 1970; Fortuin, Kasteleyn, and Ginibre 1971) <a id="pm-cite-22"></a>[[Ginibre1970](#ref-Ginibre1970), [FortuinKasteleynGinibre1971](#ref-FortuinKasteleynGinibre1971)]. The passage from local disagreement estimates to loss of boundary influence is related to disagreement percolation (Berg and Maes 1994) <a id="pm-cite-23"></a>[[VanDenBergMaes1994](#ref-VanDenBergMaes1994)]. In exact blocking, the connected polymer sums use the classical tree-graph approach to cluster expansions; a useful formulation of the Penrose identity is given by Fernández and Procacci (Fernández and Procacci 2007) <a id="pm-cite-24"></a>[[FernandezProcacci](#ref-FernandezProcacci)].

The finite-volume comparison uses reflection positivity and the chessboard method systematized by Fröhlich, Israel, Lieb and Simon (Fröhlich et al. 1978, 1980) <a id="pm-cite-25"></a>[[FILS78](#ref-FILS78), [FILS80](#ref-FILS80)]. For the final passage from Euclidean distributions to a local relativistic field, we use the reconstruction framework of Osterwalder and Schrader (Osterwalder and Schrader 1973) <a id="pm-cite-26"></a>[[OS73](#ref-OS73)] in the corrected form with the linear growth condition of (Osterwalder and Schrader 1975, sec. IV.1) <a id="pm-cite-27"></a>[[OS75](#ref-OS75)]. Reflection positivity, Euclidean covariance, clustering and the hierarchy of distributional bounds are consequently separate parts of the continuum argument.

<a id="sec:preliminary"></a>
<a id="sec:trajectories"></a>
### Construction at a fixed physical scale

<a id="pm-h-8"></a>
##### A preliminary correlation length

The first input is a mixing estimate that is uniform when bonds are weakened or deleted. Its exponential scale need not be sharp. The strict inequality in the exponent below is, however, essential to the later comparison of effective densities. We adapt the pinned-cell argument of (OpenAI 2026) <a id="pm-cite-28"></a>[[OpenAI-O4](#ref-OpenAI-O4)], retaining its current estimates and modifying the rotation algebra for spins on $S^2$.

For a bounded local Lipschitz observable $F$ with finite support $A$, set $$\mathcal L(F)=\left\lVert F\right\rVert_\infty+\max_{x\in A}\operatorname{Lip}_x(F),$$ where the individual Lipschitz constant uses round distance on $S^2$. Distances between supports are measured in the maximum norm, with the periodic distance on a torus. A finite free subgraph carries no boundary pins; bonds outside the subgraph are absent. Write $Z_b(n,w)$ for the homogeneous partition function on the rectangular $n$-by-$w$ torus, with normalized area measure at every site.

<a id="stmt-prop-preliminary"></a>
<div id="prop:preliminary" class="proposition">

<a id="eq:orig-1"></a>
**Proposition 4** (Preliminary mixing and rectangular doubling). *There are constants $b_0,C,c,p>0$ and $\eta>0$ such that, with $$X(b)=C\exp\bigl((4\pi-\eta)b\bigr),\qquad b\ge b_0,
 \label{eq:orig-1}$$ the following statements hold uniformly for all bond strengths $0\le\beta_e\le b$, including zero.*

<a id="eq:prelim-mixing"></a>
1.  *On every unpinned rectangular torus whose sides are at least $CX(b)$, and on every finite free subgraph of the square lattice, local Lipschitz observables $F,G$ supported on $A,A'$ at distance $d$ satisfy $$|\operatorname{Cov}(F,G)|\le
     C(1+b+|A|+|A'|+d)^p\mathcal L(F)\mathcal L(G)
     e^{-cd/X(b)}.
     \label{eq:prelim-mixing}$$ In the homogeneous model the periodic infinite-plane limit exists and is unique.*

<a id="eq:prelim-doubling"></a>
2.  *For each fixed aspect bound $\kappa\ge1$, the constants may be chosen so that, for even $n,w$ with $\kappa^{-1}\le n/w\le\kappa$ and $\min(n,w)\ge CX(b)$, $$0\le4\log Z_b(n,w)-\log Z_b(2n,2w)
     \le C(1+b+n+w)^p e^{-c\min(n,w)/X(b)}.
     \label{eq:prelim-doubling}$$*

</div>

The proof has three stages. We first obtain a uniform upper bound on the response of a pinned square to slowly varying rotations. A one-site estimate supplies a strict saving in the initial bound. Finally, local rotation estimates give decay for centered one-site functions, and two conditional ferromagnetic decompositions extend that decay to arbitrary local observables.

<a id="pm-h-9"></a>
###### Pinned squares, currents, and rotation identities

<a id="eq:prelim-stiffness"></a>
<a id="eq:prelim-initial-stiffness"></a>
Let $Q(S)=\{0,\ldots,S\}^2$, with arbitrary spins fixed on its boundary. Orient every bond in a positive coordinate direction. Its coefficient is $w_e=\beta_e$, except that a bond tangent to the boundary has coefficient $\beta_e/2$. This allocation makes the actions of adjacent cells add to the action of their union. For $e=x\to y$, define <a id="eq:prelim-contact"></a>$$s_e=q_x\times q_y,\qquad
 E_e=(q_x\cdot q_y)\mathbf 1-\frac12(q_xq_y^T+q_yq_x^T).
 \label{eq:prelim-contact}$$ If $F=(F_1,F_2)$ is a smooth $\mathbb C^3$-valued test field on the unit square, $z_e$ denotes the rescaled bond midpoint, and $\mu(e)$ is the bond direction, put <a id="eq:prelim-current"></a>$$\begin{aligned}
 X_Q(F)&=S^{-1}\sum_e w_es_e\cdot F_{\mu(e)}(z_e),
 \label{eq:prelim-current}\\
 \mathcal H_Q(F,G)&=
 S^{-2}\mathbb E\sum_e w_e\overline{F_{\mu(e)}(z_e)}\cdot
 E_eG_{\mu(e)}(z_e)-\operatorname{Cov}(X_Q(F),X_Q(G)).
 \label{eq:prelim-stiffness}
\end{aligned}$$ The covariance is sesquilinear, with conjugation in the first entry. The restriction of $\mathcal H_Q$ to constant $3$-by-$2$ matrices is represented by a real symmetric $6$-by-$6$ matrix $H_Q$. We call this matrix the stiffness of the pinned square. No lower bound on $H_Q$ is assumed. For a unit vector $a$, $$a^TE_ea=q_x\cdot q_y-(a\cdot q_x)(a\cdot q_y)
 =q_x^{\perp a}\cdot q_y^{\perp a},$$ so $|a^TE_ea|\le1$. The half weights give $\sum_{e\parallel\mu}w_e\le bS^2$, and consequently $$H_Q\le b\mathbf 1.
 \label{eq:prelim-initial-stiffness}$$

<a id="eq:prelim-score"></a>
<a id="eq:prelim-ward"></a>
Let $R_a(t)$ be ordinary rotation through angle $t$ about the unit axis $a$. Under $q_x\mapsto R_a(tf_x)q_x$, the action $\mathcal A=-\sum_e w_eq_x\cdot q_y$ satisfies $$D_f\mathcal A=\sum_e w_e(a\cdot s_e)(f_y-f_x),\qquad
 D_f^2\mathcal A=\sum_e w_e(a^TE_ea)(f_y-f_x)^2.
 \label{eq:prelim-score}$$ For a general infinitesimal profile $u_x\in\mathbb R^3$, direct differentiation gives <a id="eq:prelim-bond-derivative"></a>$$D_us_e=E_e(u_y-u_x)+\frac12(u_y+u_x)\times s_e.
 \label{eq:prelim-bond-derivative}$$ Thus, if $u$ vanishes on the pinned boundary and $(d_Su)_e=S(u_y-u_x)$, integration by parts yields $$\mathbb E\bigl[\overline{X_Q(d_Su)}X_Q(F)\bigr]
 =S^{-2}\mathbb E\sum_e w_e\overline{(d_Su)_e}\cdot E_eF_e
 +\frac12\mathbb EX_Q\bigl(F_e\times(\overline{u_y}+\overline{u_x})\bigr).
 \label{eq:prelim-ward}$$ Here and below the cross product is extended complex bilinearly. These are the replacements for Rloc@eq:pre:1-1Rloc@eq:pre:1-1**\[unresolved R locator: eq:pre:1-1\]**, Rloc@eq:pre:1-3Rloc@eq:pre:1-3**\[unresolved R locator: eq:pre:1-3\]**, and Rloc@eq:pre:1-5Rloc@eq:pre:1-5**\[unresolved R locator: eq:pre:1-5\]**. The current method belongs to the Ward-identity approach to spin correlations (Aizenman and Simon 1980) <a id="pm-cite-29"></a>[[AizenmanSimonWard](#ref-AizenmanSimonWard)]. The factor $1/2$ in Equation <a href="#eq:prelim-ward" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:prelim-ward">[eq:prelim-ward]</a> determines the variance gain below.

<a id="eq:prelim-size-restriction"></a>
<a id="eq:prelim-current-moment"></a>
<a id="eq:prelim-score-mgf"></a>
We use an auxiliary parameter $B\ge b$ and impose $$\log(2+S)\le16B.
 \label{eq:prelim-size-restriction}$$ For every fixed moment order $r<\infty$, the current estimate is $$\left\lVert X_Q(F)\right\rVert_{L^r}\le
 C_r(1+b)\log(2+S)\left\lVert F\right\rVert_{C^1}.
 \label{eq:prelim-current-moment}$$ We verify the change in the proof of Rloc@eq:pre:2-2Rloc@eq:pre:2-2**\[unresolved R locator: eq:pre:2-2\]**, because its uniformity in the pins will be used repeatedly. For a one-axis profile $f$ that vanishes on the boundary, Equation <a href="#eq:prelim-score" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:prelim-score">[eq:prelim-score]</a> and invariance of the product area measure give $$\mathbb Ee^{tD_f\mathcal A}
 \le\exp\left(\frac12bt^2\sum_e(f_y-f_x)^2\right).
 \label{eq:prelim-score-mgf}$$ The same Taylor estimate bounds fixed moments of the likelihood ratio of a profile rotation by $\exp(C_rb\sum_e(f_y-f_x)^2)$.

To extract a transverse current, take a patch of side $d$ with a proportional buffer, a scalar test $h$ of patch-coordinate $C^1$ norm $H_{\rm test}$, and a compact score whose potential is affine with slope $d^{-1}$ in the required spatial direction on the support of $h$. Choose its color and the rotation axis perpendicular to the desired current color. In the two opposite rotations use $$f=\arcsin(h/N),\qquad N=C\sqrt{1+b}\,H_{\rm test},$$ in place of the half angle in Rloc@pre:part-2-2Rloc@pre:part-2-2**\[unresolved R locator: pre:part-2-2\]**. Rotation of a bond current differs from rigid rotation through its midpoint angle by $O(\sup|df|)$. After multiplication by $N$, the resulting test error is $O(H_{\rm test}/d)$ per bond. There are $O(d^2)$ bonds and the score normalization is $d^{-1}$, so its deterministic cost is $CbH_{\rm test}$. Equation <a href="#eq:prelim-score-mgf" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:prelim-score-mgf">[eq:prelim-score-mgf]</a> bounds the moments of the two rotated scores, including their likelihood ratios, by $C_r(1+b)H_{\rm test}$. Hence $$\left\|d^{-1}\sum_{e\parallel\mu}w_e(s_e)_k h_e\right\|_{L^r}
 \le C_r(1+b)H_{\rm test}.$$ A Whitney decomposition of the square has $O(S/d)$ patches at each boundary-distance scale $d$. Multiplying the patch bound by $d/S$ and summing the $O(\log(2+S))$ scales proves Equation <a href="#eq:prelim-current-moment" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:prelim-current-moment">[eq:prelim-current-moment]</a>; the bounded-width boundary layer is estimated directly. This is the argument of Rloc@pre:part-2-3Rloc@pre:part-2-3**\[unresolved R locator: pre:part-2-3\]**, with constants independent of the pins and of the individual strengths.

<a id="pm-h-10"></a>
###### A uniform decrease of stiffness

The next lemma turns the local identities into a bound at a larger scale. The enlargement factor is denoted by $\ell$; it is unrelated to the fixed renormalization factor $L$ used later.

<a id="stmt-lem-prelim-iteration"></a>
<div id="lem:prelim-iteration" class="lemma">

<a id="eq:prelim-iteration-conclusion"></a>
**Lemma 5** (Stiffness iteration). *Fix a sufficiently large $D$. Suppose that, on squares of side $R$, $H_R\le h\mathbf 1$ uniformly over all boundary pins and all strengths in $[0,b]$, where $B^{-D}\le h\le B$ and $B\ge b$ is sufficiently large. The pinned-cell iteration produces a common side $R_*$ with $$H_{R_*}\le B^{-D}\mathbf 1,\qquad
 \log(R_*/R)\le4\pi h+C_D\sqrt{B\log B},
 \label{eq:prelim-iteration-conclusion}$$ provided Equation <a href="#eq:prelim-size-restriction" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:prelim-size-restriction">[eq:prelim-size-restriction]</a> holds throughout the iteration, including each proposed next square. All stiffness bounds remain uniform in the original pin and strength class.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-prelim-iteration"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-prelim-iteration</summary>

*Proof.* We give the changes to Rloc@pre:cellsRloc@pre:cells**\[unresolved R locator: pre:cells\]** through Rloc@pre:iterationRloc@pre:iteration**\[unresolved R locator: pre:iteration\]**, including the estimates that determine the coefficient $4\pi$.

<a id="eq:prelim-cell-replacement"></a>

If $Z_c(\omega)$ is the pinned partition function in cell $c$, the ring action and conditional current are $$S_g(\omega)=-\sum_c\log Z_c(\omega),\qquad

     =\ell^{-1}\sum_c\mathbb E_cX_c(F).$$ For the lower-left rescaled anchor $z_c$, put $$N_c(F)=\sup_{c^+}(|F|+\ell^{-1}|\nabla F|),\qquad

Equation <a href="#eq:prelim-current-moment" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:prelim-current-moment">[eq:prelim-current-moment]</a> gives <a id="eq:prelim-cell-bounds"></a>$$\begin{aligned}

<a id="eq:prelim-ring-hessian"></a>
For a scalar ring profile $u$, let $H_c^u$ be the cell stiffness with its pins rotated by $R_a(u)$, and put $O_c(u)=R_a(u(z_c))$, acting on the color index. Rigid covariance and Equation <a href="#eq:prelim-current-moment" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:prelim-current-moment">[eq:prelim-current-moment]</a> give <a id="eq:prelim-anchor"></a>$$\|O_c(u)^TH_c^uO_c(u)-H_c\|\le P(B)D_c(u),
